Condition: Same employee_id + month AND identical gross_pay, total_deductions and net_pay as at least one other payslip. Flagged: 'all' (all = every payslip in the group; the data cannot say which copy is the extra one).
Business reason: A person should be paid once per month.
Potential false positives: Genuine off-cycle or corrected payslips with the same amounts; when all copies are flagged, the legitimate original is flagged too.
Output flag: Potential duplicate - needs confirmation against payment/bank references (none in this dataset).

Potential false positives: Recovery of a prior overpayment could legitimately net negative.

Business reason: An employee with payable days should receive pay; fully unpaid months have payable_days = 0.
Potential false positives: Unrecorded unpaid leave or full-and-final settlement months.

Business reason: Data-dictionary identity for gross pay; breaks when an amount is mis-keyed (e.g. a shifted decimal).
Potential false positives: Rows where gross includes components not in this dataset (arrears, adjustments).

Business reason: Policy caps overtime at 50 hours and only eligible roles earn it.

Condition: pf_employee == 0 AND gross_pay > 0 AND the employee's previous-month pf_employee > 0
Business reason: PF is a statutory monthly deduction; a stop without history of exemption is suspicious.
Potential false positives: PF opt-out after a wage change; first month cannot be checked (no history).

Condition: monthly_fixed_gross < 0.99 x monthly_fixed_gross of the previous CALENDAR month (no flag if that month is missing)
Business reason: Salaries are revised upward; a drop suggests payment on the pre-revision salary.
Potential false positives: Real salary cuts/demotions; the month AFTER an erroneous spike also looks like a drop.

Business reason: A >50% one-month rise needs a promotion record; none exists in this dataset.

Condition: monthly_fixed_gross > 2.0 x median monthly_fixed_gross of the same role_id in the previous calendar month
Business reason: Pay should be close to the prior month's role norm; double is a role/grade mismatch candidate.
Potential false positives: Genuine outliers (rare skills, retention packages); roles with very few holders.

Condition: Any required money / day column is NaN or non-finite
Business reason: A payslip with a missing or invalid amount cannot be trusted.
Potential false positives: Intentionally blank optional fields (none among required columns).
